$comment: A ledger with zero entries, on purpose. Read this before concluding something is missing.
why_this_file_exists: tests/attention/test_broker_journal_contract.py is quarantined in interlock by a module-level pytest.importorskip('claude_org_runtime.broker.server') (interlock#39), so pytest collects NO node id from it. It contributes nothing to the 2,194 and nothing to the attention subsystem's 194.

It therefore cannot have a normal ledger: parity/parity-check.mjs's first act on a ledger is to read the per-file inventory it points at, and there is no inventory file to point at -- an empty one could not be told apart from a generation failure, and a fabricated node id would be a case that does not exist (parity/source-inventory.manifest.json's collection_time_skips records it instead).

D-0034 ratified that the file nevertheless gets a standalone, metadata-only ledger recording zero entries, outside the parity checker's normal file-to-inventory linkage: an explicit, checked-in 'this file contributes nothing' rather than the file's total absence from every attention ledger being mistaken for an oversight.

not_registered_in.why: Deliberate, and named in a comment beside the attention lane there so the omission is visible at the place a reader would look for it. Registering this file would make the checker read an inventory that does not exist.

file.reason: Quarantined by interlock#39: the carried invariants in this file are kept verbatim, but they drive broker/server.py, which interlock's PORTING_LEDGER.md classes discard. Re-target onto the MessageBus rewrite (interlock Q-0023).

belongs_to.where_the_status_lives: parity/source-inventory.belts.md, the `broker` section -- which is `not-porting` (ratified 2026-09-03, D-0053). The section used to read `retarget`, meaning the invariants carry but drive broker/server.py so a port would have to re-point them onto a continuo mechanism first, and it used to say the re-pointing was still open at continuo's human gate. The gate has now sat, and `retarget` turned out to be the wrong single word for two questions with different answers: D-0053 DECLINES the 54 collected cases of tests/broker/test_residents.py (the residents registry is written by the consumer, not the runtime, and `grep -rni resident src/ test/` over this repository returns zero -- there is no subject on either side of the port), and DISCHARGES the five uncollected modules, this file among them, at BELT level rather than case by case. What discharges them is that D-0032 had already named the messagebus package as their destination and that belt is complete at 43 of 43, so interlock's own instruction -- Q-0023, `re-target onto the MessageBus rewrite`, quoted verbatim in `source.file.reason` above and still the correct reading of the source -- is answered by the rewrite existing. A per-case retarget was never merely expensive, it was UNAVAILABLE: with no node ids there are no cases to retarget, and nothing may be invented in their place. That is also why D-0053 leaves this ledger exactly as it is: what stops this file having a normal ledger is the absence of an inventory to point at, which the decision does not change, so D-0034's metadata-only zero-entry ledger stands unchanged and is not converted into anything. interlock is frozen and answers Q-0023 for nobody (D-0036), so nothing here was ever waiting on it and nothing here is waiting now. The `attention` section of that document says the same thing from the other side, so a reader arriving from either place is told this file is not one of the 194.
belongs_to.not_this_belt: A1 ports tests/attention/test_readers.py (29) and tests/attention/test_classifier.py (61). This file is neither, and no case of it is ported, deferred or waived here -- there is no case of it to do any of those to.

target_only_tests.why: Nothing is ported from this file, so nothing sits beside it.
